questions.q: Which of the following is incorrect?
options: Primary alcohols are very easily oxidised to aldehydes, which are oxidised to acids with same number of C-atoms.
Secondary alcohols are very easily oxidised to ketones, which are oxidised to acids with same number of C-atoms.
Secondary alcohols are easily oxidised to ketones, which are oxidised to acids with lesser number of C-atoms.
Secondary and tertiary alcohols on oxidation form acids with lesser number of C-atoms.
questions.solution:
Primary alcohols are easily oxidised to aldehydes and then to acid, both containing the same number of carbon atoms, while secondary alcohols are easily oxidised to ketones with same number of carbon atoms, but ketone oxidised to carboxylic acid containing lesser number of carbon atoms than original alcohol.
Thus all alcohols on oxidation finally give acids but acids obtained from $2^{\circ}$ and $3^{\circ}$ alcohols contain less C-atom.

questions.q: Which of these represents the correct order of decreasing bond order?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{He}_2^{+}: \sigma 1 s^2, \sigma 1 s^1 \\
& \mathrm{BO}=\frac{1}{2}\left(N_b-N_a\right)=\frac{1}{2}(2-1)=\frac{1}{2}=0.5 \\
& \mathrm{C}_2^{2-}: \sigma 1 s^2, \sigma^* 1 s^2, \sigma 2 s^2, \sigma^* 2 s^2,\left(\pi 2 p_x^2 \approx \pi 2 p_y^2\right), \sigma 2 p_z^2 \\
& \mathrm{BO}=\frac{1}{2}(10-4)=\frac{6}{2}=3.0 \\

& \mathrm{BO}=\frac{1}{2}(10-5)=\frac{5}{2}=2.5 \\

& \mathrm{BO}=\frac{1}{2}(10-7)=\frac{3}{2}=1.5 \quad\left(\pi^* 2 p_x^2 \approx \pi^* 2 p_y^1\right)\end{aligned}$

questions.q: At $300 \mathrm{~K}$, the half-life period of a gaseous reaction at an initial pressure of $40 \mathrm{kPa}$ is 350 s. When pressure is $20 \mathrm{kPa}$, the half-life period is $175 \mathrm{~s}$. What is the order of the reaction?
questions.solution:
We know that
$\frac{\left(t_{1 / 2}\right)_1}{\left(t_{1 / 2}\right)_2}=\left(\frac{p_2}{p_1}\right)^{n-1}$
where, $n$ is the order of reaction and $t_{1 / 2}$ is half-life.
$\begin{gathered}
\frac{350}{175}=\left(\frac{20}{40}\right)^{n-1} \\
2=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{n-1} \\
\Rightarrow n-1=-1 \\
n=0
\end{gathered}\therefore$ It is a zero order reaction.

On differentiating the equation, $y=x^2-x y$ w.r.t. $x$, we

& \text { get } \frac{d y}{d x}=2 x-\left(x \frac{d y}{d x}+y\right) \\

& \Rightarrow\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)_{(1,1 / 2)}=\frac{2(1)-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)}{1+(1)}=\frac{3 / 2}{2}=\frac{3}{4}

questions.solution:
Due to the specific shape of wings, when the aeroplane runs, air passes at higher speed over it as compared to its lower surface. This difference of air speeds above and below the wings, in accordance with Bernoulli's principle, creates a pressure difference, due to which an upward force called 'dynamic lift' acts on the plate.
$\therefore$ Upward lift $=$ pressure difference \times  area of the wings
$[\because F=p \times A]$
From Bernoulli's equation,
$\begin{aligned}
p_1+\frac{1}{2} \rho v_1{ }^2 & =p_2+\frac{1}{2} \rho v_2{ }^2 \\
\because \quad p_2-p_1 & =\frac{1}{2} \rho\left(v_1{ }^2-v_2{ }^2\right) \\
\text { Hence, upward lift } & =\frac{1}{2} \rho A\left(v_1^2-v_2^2\right)
\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:

and ratio in their lengths,

When same force is applied on them, then ratio change in their lengths,
$\frac{\Delta l_1}{\Delta l_2}=\text { ? }$
We known that, Young's modulus,
$\begin{gathered}
Y=\frac{F l}{A \Delta l} \Rightarrow \Delta l=\frac{F l}{A Y} \\
\Delta l \propto \frac{l}{A} \\
\therefore \quad \frac{\Delta l_1}{\Delta l_2}=\frac{l_1 / A_1}{l_2 / A_2}=\frac{l_1 A_2}{l_2 A_2} \\
\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\Delta l_1}{\Delta l_2}=\frac{l_1 / A_1}{r_2^2 / r_1^2}=\frac{1}{2} \cdot\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2=\frac{1}{8}
\end{gathered}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body is projected vertically upwards. The times corresponding to height $h$ while ascending and while descending are $t_1$ and $t_2$, respectively. Then, the velocity of projection will be (take, $g$ as acceleration due to gravity)
questions.solution:
Let $v$ be initial velocity of vertical projection and $t$ be the time taken by the body to reach a height $h$ from ground.
Here, $\quad u=u, a=-g, s=h, t=t$
Using,
$s=u t+\frac{1}{2} a t^2$, we have
$\begin{aligned}
& h=u t+\frac{1}{2}(-g) t^2 \\
& g t^2-2 u t+2 h=0 \\
& t=\frac{2 u \pm \sqrt{4 u^2-4 g \times 2 h}}{2 g}=\frac{u \pm \sqrt{u^2-2 g h}}{g}
\end{aligned}$
It means $t$ has two values, i.e.
$\begin{aligned}
t_1 & =\frac{u+\sqrt{u^2-2 g h}}{g} \Rightarrow t_2=\frac{u-\sqrt{u^2-2 g h}}{g} \\
t_1+t_2 & =\frac{2 u}{g} \text { or } u=\frac{g\left(t_1+t_2\right)}{2}
\end{aligned}$
